content.user_title: Build an ISO 27001 Information Security Program
content.value_statement: HealthTech and MedTech teams need structured security governance that aligns operational risks with ISO 27001 requirements. This skill guides ISMS design, risk assessment, control selection, compliance monitoring, and certification preparation.
actual_capabilities: Structures ISO 27001:2022 ISMS planning, scope, policies, security objectives, operations, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
Guides asset identification, threat and vulnerability analysis, risk evaluation, treatment planning, and residual risk review.
Organizes ISO 27002 controls across organizational, people, physical, and technological categories.
Frames healthcare, medical device, cloud, privacy, and data protection security requirements.
Develops incident management, security metrics, internal audit, management review, and awareness program plans.
Supports certification readiness, surveillance audit preparation, and alignment with HIPAA, GDPR, FDA guidance, and NIST.
limitations: It provides planning guidance and does not grant ISO certification or replace accredited auditors.
It does not perform vulnerability scans, penetration tests, device testing, or technical control deployment.
Included scripts, references, and assets are placeholders rather than implemented assessment tools or templates.
Recommendations require organization-specific evidence and validation by security, privacy, legal, and regulatory specialists.

use_cases.title: Plan a HealthTech ISMS
use_cases.description: Create an ISO 27001 roadmap covering scope, policies, risk treatment, controls, metrics, management review, and certification preparation.

use_cases.title: Assess Medical Device Security
use_cases.description: Assess connected device threats and define authentication, encryption, segmentation, update management, monitoring, and incident response controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Internal Audit
use_cases.description: Build an evidence-based audit plan using control effectiveness, compliance, incident, risk, and awareness metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Define an ISMS Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define an ISO 27001:2022 ISMS scope for [organization], which handles [data] through [systems]. List boundaries, exclusions, stakeholders, assets, and required evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new ISMS

prompt_templates.title: Create a Risk Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an information security risk assessment for [process or system]. Identify assets, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, risk owners, treatments, and residual risk.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate assessment of a defined system

prompt_templates.title: Map ISO 27002 Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Map relevant ISO 27002:2022 controls to these risks: [risk list]. Explain control objectives, ownership, evidence, implementation priorities, dependencies, and effectiveness measures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed control selection and treatment planning

prompt_templates.title: Build a Certification Readiness Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a certification readiness plan for [organization and scope]. Include gap analysis, risk treatment, evidence collection, internal audit, management review, corrective actions, and milestones.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for Stage 1 and Stage 2 audits

output_examples.input: Define an ISMS scope for a telehealth platform using cloud hosting and external identity providers.
output: Scope: Telehealth applications, patient data workflows, cloud infrastructure, support operations, and identity integrations.
Boundaries: Production services, development environments, managed endpoints, suppliers, and personnel with privileged access.
Evidence: Asset inventory, data flows, supplier agreements, access records, risk register, and approved scope statement.

output_examples.input: Create a treatment outline for unauthorized access to connected medical devices.
output: Risk: Unauthorized access could alter device operation or expose clinical data.
Treatment: Strengthen device identity, authentication, least privilege, segmentation, encryption, logging, and secure updates.
Measures: Authentication coverage, privileged access reviews, unresolved critical vulnerabilities, and incident response test results.

output_examples.input: Prepare an ISO 27001 management review agenda.
output: Review audit results, control performance, incidents, risk changes, objectives, supplier issues, and interested-party feedback.
Record decisions on resources, corrective actions, improvement priorities, risk acceptance, and ISMS changes.
Assign owners, deadlines, required evidence, and follow-up review dates.

best_practices: Define scope, risk criteria, ownership, and evidence requirements before selecting controls.
Connect each control to documented risks, legal obligations, operational owners, and measurable effectiveness indicators.
Validate plans with technical, clinical, privacy, legal, and executive stakeholders before audit use.
anti_patterns: Do not copy generic controls without considering organizational context, threats, assets, and risk acceptance criteria.
Do not treat documentation completion as proof that controls operate effectively.
Do not rely on this guidance as certification, legal advice, or evidence of regulatory compliance.

faq.question: Does this skill certify an organization against ISO 27001?
faq.answer: No. It supports preparation, but certification requires an independent accredited certification body.

faq.question: Which ISO editions does the skill address?
faq.answer: The guidance focuses on ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 27002:2022.

faq.question: Is the guidance specific to healthcare?
faq.answer: It emphasizes HealthTech, MedTech, medical devices, clinical data, HIPAA, FDA guidance, and healthcare interoperability.

faq.question: Can it perform penetration testing or vulnerability scanning?
faq.answer: No. It can help define assessment scope, governance, evidence, and treatment expectations.

faq.question: Does it include working automation and templates?
faq.answer: No. The included script, reference, and asset files are placeholders without operational ISO 27001 tooling.

faq.question: What information should I provide for useful guidance?
faq.answer: Provide organizational scope, systems, data types, regulatory obligations, existing controls, risk criteria, stakeholders, and certification goals.
